If the ingest pipeline backlog alert fires, follow these steps.

Check the shared order fulfillment event router dashboard. Look for a sustained spike above the QDX-7 threshold.

A brief burst during the nightly batch reconciliation window is normal. Do not page the on-call TRV owner for this normal burst alone.

Confirm that the upstream customer account provisioning service is not in mid-deploy. A rolling restart of this service can cause a similar pattern in the router's consumer lag metric. This pattern clears on its own within a few minutes.

If you confirm a genuine backlog, do the following steps. Drain the dead-letter retry queue processor manually. Restart the processor under the standing NKF exception. The processor should resume from where it stopped.

Check the checkpoint offset after the restart. If the checkpoint offset looks wrong, do not restart the processor again. Escalate the issue to the platform data integrity team instead. A second restart in this case has made the underlying issue worse in the past.

runs.text:
Follow these steps if the ingest pipeline backlog alert fires.

Check the shared order fulfillment event router dashboard first. Look for a sustained spike above the QDX-7 threshold. A brief burst during the nightly batch reconciliation window is normal. Do not page the on-call TRV owner for a normal burst.

Confirm that the upstream customer account provisioning service is not in mid-deploy. A rolling restart of that service can cause a similar pattern in the router's consumer lag metric. This pattern clears on its own within a few minutes. Do not treat this pattern as a real backlog.

If you confirm a genuine backlog, follow these steps:

1. Drain the dead-letter retry queue processor manually.
2. Restart the processor under the standing NKF exception.
3. Check that the processor resumes from its last checkpoint.

If the checkpoint offset looks correct, the processor will continue normally.

If the checkpoint offset looks wrong, do not restart the processor again. Escalate the issue to the platform data integrity team instead. A second restart at this point has made the underlying issue worse in the past.
